title: State-of-the-art global models underestimate impacts from climate extremes
problem: The ability of state-of-the-art global impact models to capture the severe, multi-sectoral impacts of extreme climate events is largely untested, with this paper showing that most models systematically underestimate the extremeness of these impacts in sectors like agriculture, ecosystems, and human health.
method: The paper proposes a systematic, multi-sectoral evaluation of global impact models by comparing their simulated outputs against observed impacts from a historical analogue, the 2003 European heat wave and drought, to test how well the models capture the effects of extreme climate conditions.
task: The task is to test how well state-of-the-art global impact models capture the multi-sectoral impacts of extreme climate events, using the 2003 European heat wave and drought as a case study.

obs_and_metrics.result: The multi-model median closely reproduced large negative anomalies (~1.5-2σ) in the Rhine, Tisza, Danube, and Aare rivers, but overestimated more moderate anomalies in the Elbe and Oder rivers.

obs_and_metrics.model: Ensemble of 12 global gridded crop models
obs_and_metrics.result: In countries with the largest negative anomalies (France, Italy), the impacts were underestimated by most or all models. In 3 of 5 strongly impacted countries, all models underestimated the anomaly.

obs_and_metrics.model: Ensemble of 12 global gridded crop models
obs_and_metrics.result: Large anomalies in France and Italy were underestimated by the entire ensemble. In 7 of 9 strongly impacted countries, more than 75% of models underestimated the anomaly.
The observed negative GPP anomaly was underestimated by all models in the West region (France/Spain) and by 75% of models in the Central region.

obs_and_metrics.observational_dataset: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) annual generation data
obs_and_metrics.result: Simulated anomalies were close to observed ones for Italy and the UK. In 3 of 9 countries with an observed negative anomaly larger than 1σ, the model underestimates the magnitude of the anomaly.

obs_and_metrics.observational_dataset: Published literature based on city mortality data
obs_and_metrics.result: Estimates were consistent with observations for Barcelona, London, and Rome, but substantially underestimated the magnitude of the impact in 5 out of 8 cities, including Paris, Milan, and Turin.

innovation: This paper provides the first systematic, multi-sectoral test of how well global impact models capture extreme climate events, revealing that most models substantially underestimate the observed impacts of the 2003 European heatwave on agriculture, ecosystems, and human mortality, suggesting societal risks are greater than previously thought.
